entrypoints.summary: A consumer supplies a crafted progressive, arithmetically encoded JPEG to the TurboJPEG decompressor; the report's embedded C program invokes tjDecompress2() on its constructed image.

affected_components.role: The report identifies the MCU handler-selection condition and demonstrates the public TurboJPEG decompression call; the actual audited source file and revision are absent.

negative_controls: When preserving error tolerance, skip bogus scans that provide no additional information.
observability.positive_marker: The report records tjDecompress2() running for six hours on an Intel i7 for the supplied 8192x8192, 8 MB case.

preconditions: The consuming application accepts attacker-controlled JPEG input.
The JPEG is progressive and arithmetically encoded.

sources.concept: attacker-controlled progressive arithmetic JPEG with repeated SOS-only scans

impact.affected_asset: Availability of the process or service performing JPEG decompression.
impact.attacker_capability: Cause a libjpeg-turbo consumer to spend disproportionate time decoding an attacker-supplied JPEG.
impact.security_effect: Denial of service through excessive CPU time during image decompression.

causal_trace.summary: An attacker constructs a progressive arithmetic JPEG containing structural markers and repeated SOS-only scan segments, with no image data for the scans.

After the arithmetic scan decoder encounters a marker, later requests for scan input are fulfilled with zero bytes until scan completion; the report describes multiple scan segments as short as 10 bytes and an arbitrary number of them.
The crafted scan parameters select decode_mcu_DC_refine() (Ah non-zero and Ss zero), rather than handlers with a fast path for zero-stuffed input, so the decoder processes each bogus scan.
Although JWRN_BOGUS_PROGRESSION is reported, it is not an error by default and every scan is fully decoded; the report observed tjDecompress2() run for six hours for its 8192x8192, 8 MB construction.

failure.operation: Full decoding of repeated bogus progressive arithmetic scans after zero-filled input continuation

primary_invariant.kind: bounded decoding work for malformed or incomplete progressive arithmetic scans
primary_invariant.statement: A decoder warning for bogus progression should prevent full decoding of scan segments that supply no additional information, so compact malformed input cannot impose disproportionate decode work.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The decoder continues after JWRN_BOGUS_PROGRESSION and supplies zero bytes through scan completion; repeated short SOS-only segments are then fully processed through the DC-refinement handler.

raw_refs.role: versioned Cure53 audit report and embedded reproducer

quality.review_notes: The primary audit report was inspected and contains the finding narrative, handler-selection conditions, embedded C construction program, an observed runtime result, and recommendations. No immutable audited source checkout, fix commit, release range, regression test, or execution artifact for a remediation is in the bundle. The current upstream repository homepage is not treated as historical code evidence.

remediation.invariant_restored: Bogus progressive scans no longer receive full decoding work after the bogus-progression condition; decoding either aborts or omits non-informative scans.
mitigation_classes: skip bogus scans that add no information when error tolerance is required

state_context.attacker_state_setup: Use a progressive arithmetic frame with attacker-selected dimensions and repeated SOS-only scan segments; set Ah non-zero and Ss zero.
data_structure_invariants: Bogus progression should not cause every non-informative scan to be fully decoded.
Decoder work should remain bounded when scan input ends at a marker and synthetic zero input is used.

numeric_domains.attacker_constraints: The report states dimensions are attacker chosen, possibly constrained by the consuming application; its example uses 8192x8192.
numeric_domains.name: frame dimensions

numeric_domains.attacker_constraints: The report describes SOS-only progressive arithmetic scan segments as short as 10 bytes and permits repeated segments.
numeric_domains.name: scan segment length

state_context.state_machine: Arithmetic-scan decoding encounters a marker, then continues satisfying arithmetic-decoder input requests with zero bytes until scan completion; crafted progressive scan parameters select DC refinement.

affected_versions_or_commits.value: The report identifies libjpeg-turbo but the supplied artifacts do not establish an audited source revision, affected release range, or fixed release.

oracle.expected_negative: With the recommended abort behavior, decoding terminates at bogus progression; with the tolerant alternative, bogus scans that provide no additional information are skipped rather than fully decoded.
oracle.expected_positive: The report's embedded generator produces a progressive arithmetic JPEG for which tjDecompress2() continues decoding bogus scans and exhibits very long completion time; the report records six hours on an Intel i7 for the stated construction.
